decision: when run as root, the copy's programs run as an unprivileged account (postgres system user, else nobody)
why: PostgreSQL refuses root and this session runs as root; this narrows, not widens, what the server can touch

decision: no needs-owner issue for the environment: PostgreSQL 16.15 and PostgREST 12.2.12 are installed and a probe copy answered a real read
why: every scenario can be shown here

decision: fix-round T-01
why: verifier FAIL at 85fbc7a: D-1 extension guard and D-2 settings check and direct view resolve catalog names under a search_path the migrations control

decision: migrations and the direct view go through pg.py, a small client of PostgreSQL's simple query protocol, not psql
why: psql runs backslash commands inside a migration file (\! runs a shell command on the machine)

decision: migrations are cut into statements by rlsentry (quotes, dollar quotes, comments, BEGIN ATOMIC) and run one by one, each file in one transaction, as the Supabase CLI does; design said never split SQL
why: a refused COPY TO file carries no error position, so only per-statement runs can name the statement; a wrong cut only fails, which stops the run

decision: the database listens on no TCP port, only its socket in the run's 0700 directory with local trust; PostgREST connects through the socket and is the only loopback port
why: trust on a loopback TCP port would let any local user in as superuser

decision: runs live in <tmp>/rlsentry-runs-<uid>/; each run's record (<id>.json) sits beside its directory, written first
why: a per-user root avoids sharing /tmp with other users; the server's account owns the directory, so it must not be able to edit which pids a later run kills

decision: the copy's processes are found by working directory, and dead runs' servers stopped with SIGQUIT
why: PostgreSQL's backends each call setsid(), so process groups do not reach them

decision: role postgres gets ADMIN on anon, authenticated, service_role, authenticator, owns database postgres, and has GRANT SET on PostgREST's in-database parameters (pgrst.*)
why: as on Supabase, a migration may make these settings, so the settings check names them; without the grants PostgreSQL 16 refuses them and the stop would only be a failed statement; a pgrst.* name not on the list still fails as a statement

decision: Supabase's setup followed is supabase/postgres 15.8.1.x; auth.users carries its full column list, not only the design's subset; the setup puts no setting on anon/authenticated/authenticator (Supabase sets statement_timeout on them)
why: migrations' triggers name many auth.users columns; any such setting would stop every run under the brief's rule

decision: postgres and initdb are looked up on PATH first, else in pg_config --bindir; postgrest on PATH
why: Debian/Ubuntu keep postgres off PATH; PATH first lets S-7's stand-in work

decision: the server's version and PostgREST's Server header are what the reports keep; --version only gates the build
why: brief: where the two differ the server decides

decision: Ctrl-C exits 130 and SIGTERM 143-style via the same path, after the copy is destroyed; the copy's programs run in their own sessions
why: the brief names no code for an interrupt; own sessions keep a terminal's Ctrl-C from reaching the server mid-cleanup

decision: until T-02 a run that reaches the end prints the exposed schemas' tables with row-level security on/off and exits 0
why: the ticket asks the run to report the tables found; RLS on/off makes the plain-folder ordering visible in the direct view

decision: config.toml is read with tomllib, with tomli as a runtime dependency on Python 3.10 only
why: tomllib is in the standard library from 3.11; the brief allows 3.10

decision: test_command is python3 -m pytest -q, after pip install -e .[test]
why: the suite is the S-10 harness

decision: a migration failure shows the server's detail and hint as well as its message
why: the detail names the missing role (e.g. pg_execute_server_program), which says why it was refused

decision: the superuser's connections send back, at startup, the server's value (read through template1) of every setting a migration made on database postgres, and search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp; not a fixed list of settings
why: the migrations' role owns the database, so role, search_path, read-only and any other setting it makes would reach the superuser; alter database postgres set role = anon made the superuser's reads run as anon

decision: the overrides leave out the settings the database keeps for PostgREST's own connections: those still behave as the project's would (as on Supabase), and only the settings check judges them
why: the copy should behave like the project; only rlsentry's own reads must be shielded

decision: the extension guard refuses a null name as well as pinning its search_path; the null check cannot be reached by a migration once the catalog is named in full, so it is defence only
why: failing closed costs nothing; it was seen to refuse when the qualification was removed

decision: design: the settings check moves after seeding, right before PostgREST starts
why: seeding runs the migrations' triggers, which made settings the check had already passed; the design's order caused T-02's defect

decision: fix-round T-02
why: verifier FAIL at 1960dc8: a trigger run by seeding makes role and pgrst.* settings after the settings check

decision: JSON field names for a read without a verdict: per attempt `key` ("anon key"/"no key"), `status` (HTTP status, null when no answer), `error_code` (PostgreSQL SQLSTATE from the body's `code`, else null), `rows`, `reason`; per outcome `reason` when no request was sent
why: the brief leaves the names to the builder; T-03 renders the JSON from these report.Result fields

decision: a timeout leaves that table without a verdict and the remaining tables are still read (exit 2 at the end); it does not stop the run at once
why: the brief's "How a run goes" and the ticket put a timeout among the no-verdict cases; the Assumptions line saying a timeout stops the run is read as that end-of-run stop

decision: a table with no columns gets no verdict ("the table has no columns; no request sent") rather than a stop at once
why: the ticket lists it among the no-verdict cases

decision: the checks before any request run in this order: no columns, then no usage on the schema (names the schema, S-4), then no column anon may read
why: S-4 says the stop names the schema even when the select grant is missing too

decision: new part direct.py (the direct view: tables, readable columns, schema usage, not-reachable tables, rows); the design table gains its row
why: cli.py would otherwise hold catalog SQL; seeding and the attack share it

decision: the direct view renders a value with to_json only when its type, through domains and arrays, is owned by the superuser; otherwise it uses the type's output function as a JSON string; answer and view are compared as parsed JSON with numbers kept as text
why: to_json calls a cast to json made by the migrations on their own types, as the superuser; an output function cannot be replaced by a non-superuser

decision: known limit: a column whose type is a composite made by the migrations, or whose rendering PostgREST's session formats differently (a TimeZone or DateStyle set on the database), is answered differently from the direct view and stops the run as "rows the table does not hold"
why: a false stop costs a stop, never a false verdict; widening the comparison needs probing each case

decision: seeding fills every insertable column, those with defaults too (uuid and now() defaults included), with fixed fake values; it uses the column defaults only when a row is refused
why: uuid or now() defaults would make the evidence differ between two runs

decision: known limit for T-03: a value a trigger fills from the clock (an updated_at trigger) still differs between runs and shows in the evidence
why: seeding cannot stop a trigger from setting it; T-03 owns "two runs give the same report"
evidence: driven check in the Ready comment of #28

decision: seeding covers every table of an exposed schema plus every table their foreign keys reach, auth.users first; parents before children; a cycle is broken in name order; a refused row is retried up to 6 ways (other parent, other fake values, defaults, a named value, nulls) and then left out
why: the design's "bounded tries"; parents outside the exposed schemas must hold rows for the children to point at

decision: the anon key's made-up claims are fixed (ref rlsentrycopy000000000, iat 1700000000, exp 4102444800), signed with the per-run secret
why: two runs send the same requests; only the secret must be secret

decision: an unexpected error of rlsentry's own exits 2 with a "failed:" message, never 1 or 0
why: before this a crash exited 1, which a script reads as "exposed" (seen during the build on a bad catalog query)

decision: evidence is the direct-view row (on the columns read) that sorts first by its JSON text, among the rows either request got; rows_read counts the distinct rows either got, and rows_held the rows the table held
why: makes the evidence the same on every run

decision: twelve T-01 tests updated to the exit codes and output the reads now give (1 for exposed, 2 for no verdict); what each proves is unchanged
why: T-01's interim run printed tables and always exited 0
evidence: tests/test_inputs.py, test_settings.py, test_supabase_migrations.py, test_lifecycle.py, test_versions.py, test_boundary.py

decision: the settings check runs after seeding, right before PostgREST starts; a stop for a setting now comes after seeding instead of before it
why: seeding runs the migrations' triggers as their role, the last migration code that can run before the reads; the reads are read-only (25006), so nothing later can make a setting

decision: no new test for a policy function that makes a setting during a read: PostgREST's read-only transaction refuses it, and rlsentry has no switch that a test could break to watch that test fail
why: a test that cannot be seen to fail proves nothing; the verifier saw 405/25006 on both reads
